title: Trapping Rain Water
description: You are given n non-negative integers representing the heights of bars in an elevation map, where every bar has width 1. Compute how much water can be trapped between the bars after it rains.
inputFormat:
Line 1: an integer n, the number of bars.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, the heights.
outputFormat: A single integer, the total units of trapped water.
hints: The water above one bar depends on the tallest bar to its left and the tallest bar to its right.
The water above a bar is the smaller of those two heights minus the bar's own height.
You can avoid extra arrays by moving two pointers inward from both ends.

examples.explanation: 6 units of water are trapped between the bars.
The low bars in the middle hold 9 units in total.
